animals/bee: "huddles with its colony to keep warm through winter": true of honeybees (the ordinary sense); bumblebee colonies die off and only the queens overwinter
"can sting, though some kinds die after doing so": honeybee workers die after stinging mammals because the barbed sting tears out; other bees survive
animals/deer: "bounds away with its white tail raised when startled": characteristic of white-tailed deer; other species (roe, red deer) flash a pale rump patch rather than raising a white tail
"has a reddish-brown summer coat that turns greyer in winter": true of white-tailed, roe and red deer; not all species
"often has a spotted coat when it is very young": most fawns are spotted, but moose and reindeer calves are not
animals/dolphin: "can sleep with one half of its brain at a time": well documented (unihemispheric sleep) but may not be common knowledge for a lay reader
animals/frog: "can spend winter dormant in the mud of pond bottoms": true of some kinds (e.g. leopard and green frogs, which mostly rest on the bottom rather than burrow deep); others overwinter on land
animals/mouse: "eats seeds and grains, sometimes storing them in its nest": food caching is well known in field and deer mice; house mice cache less
"can squeeze through gaps the width of a pencil": commonly cited pest-control figure (about 6-7 mm) for house mice
animals/sheep: "greatly outnumbers the human population of New Zealand": true now (roughly five to one) but the ratio has been falling for decades
animals/snake: "often sheds its whole skin in a single piece": typical of healthy snakes; a poor shed comes off in patches
animals/tiger: "is a national emblem in India and Bangladesh": the Bengal tiger is the national animal of both; the checker allows "national" (the family word is only "nation(s)"), but a reader may see it as near the countries family word
animals/wolf: "has yellow or amber eyes that stand out against its fur": typical of adult wolves; eye colour varies somewhat
